The old event-delta table lacks its script and sample IDs, so novelty is only relative to reconstructable samples. ALL validation was summary-exposed. Full selected-row fingerprint screen: 960,000 train and 480,000 validation rows; cross-split matching sequence pairs: 0. This checks unchanged 112-feature float32 row identity only. Unsampled or transformed linked chains remain unknown. No independence interval is claimed. Scored rows: 31,658. Scores pool rows globally with abs(clipped target) weights. All-required scores diagnose mask sensitivity.

ECONOMETRICS CONTINUATION — ECO_CLOCK_01 / ECO_CLOCK_02 Verdict: general event-clock superiority FAILED both frozen gates. Retain the negative. Target-specific clock behavior is a narrow candidate for later controls. RECOVERY RECOVERY_SUMMARY.txt was written before scoring. Own saved target ACF shows persistence for hundreds of rows and negative cross-target correlation, with four lattice spacings. Targets are unavailable online: this is not evidence for a label-AR predictor. event_delta_corr.txt is exploratory, lacks sample/script provenance, and relates contemporaneous target changes to feature changes. That relationship cannot identify a causal market mechanism or future signal. No other analyst findings, campaign models, or strong baseline were inspected. METHOD AND CAUSALITY 48 training sequences, 24 validation sequences, uniformly seeded selection. Train groups exclude lattice300, train0, and inferred seed2 ACF120; the NPZ has 120 sequences but does not store original group IDs. Unknown event-delta training exposure prevents claiming fully fresh training. ALL validation was already exposed in own valid_seq_summary.csv. Followup uses the same now score-exposed IDs. Each sequence is streamed independently; only its current/past 112 raw features enter models. 22 i0 price columns are used without assuming depth ordering. Rows 0–98 update history; all state resets at sequence boundaries. No targets, mask, full-sequence lattice, or IDs are inputs. Global feature scaling is fit on training only. Prefix/full feature parity at 777 rows: maximum difference 0. Training: every tenth required row, 95,568 samples. Validation: 31,658 exact need_prediction AND is_scored rows. Predict every required row regardless of mask. Target-specific ridge minimizes abs(clipped target)-weighted squared error; penalty = 0.01 mean non-intercept standardized Gram diagonal. Intercept unpenalized. All scoring clips finite targets/predictions to +/-2 and pools additive moments across sequences before computing target-wise correlations and their equal mean. No row bootstrap, confidence interval, independent replication, or public forecast. PROBES ACTUALLY RUN ECO_CLOCK_01 frozen before execution, 12.38 seconds CPU-scope wall time. All history arms add exactly 22 columns to raw112. alpha=2/33. Row EMA updates every row; event EMA updates on any i0 price-column change and holds otherwise. Stale control delays event displacement by 4,096 rows with zeros before then. Shared training row-history scaling is a potential shrinkage confound, corrected in the followup. Frozen gate: event-row >0.002 and positive on both targets. Arm t0 WP t1 WP mean WP all-required mean WP raw 0.559806 0.563620 0.561713 0.329477 row_clock 0.571423 0.565269 0.568346 0.323630 event_clock 0.563712 0.571894 0.567803 0.329944 stale_event 0.555111 0.559696 0.557404 0.326711 Event minus row = -0.000544; t0 -0.007712, t1 +0.006624; 11/24 sequence wins. Recent history helps this local raw-feature ridge, but stale history hurts. The event-specific gate FAILED; do not report the raw-control gain as proof. ECO_CLOCK_02 adaptively proposed, separately frozen before execution, 23.86 sec. Same train/valid IDs, features, fit rows and regularization rule. Each arm now uses its own training feature mean/std. Hazard clock updates every row with alpha_t = 1-(1-2/33)^q_t, where q_t=(24.75+prior price events)/(99+prior rows). This approximates expected event-time decay from causal prefix frequency. It controls slow quiet-period smoothing, but not the entire realized age distribution. Frozen both-target gate FAILED. The average delta is driven by t1. This contradicts a common-clock assumption and favors testing target-specific history, not universal event time. Followup event-row mean remains -0.000365. All-required ordering differs: row history lowers the mean by -0.005847 versus raw; event improves only +0.000398. The exact mask selects a different statistical population. No propensity or mask-training correction was fitted here; diagnostic sensitivity is not test gain. SAMPLE PROVENANCE AND DEPENDENCE cache/continuation_manifest.json lists all row groups, actual IDs, prior exposed groups, feature order, dataset file sizes/mtime/schema SHA256 and frozen-contract hash. Full selected-row raw112 fingerprint screening compared 960,000 train rows with 480,000 valid rows: ZERO exact cross-split matches (128-bit BLAKE2b). All 960,000 training raw rows had distinct fingerprints. This rules out unchanged shared raw rows within these selected sequences, subject to negligible hash risk. It does NOT exclude transformed overlaps, unsampled linked sequences, or campaign exposure. Campaign connected-component mapping remains an integration blocker. Per-sequence paired deltas are descriptive; no independence inference is claimed. Actual sequence IDs are included below and machine-readable in the manifest. FIGURES INSPECTED fig/target_acf.png: old target persistence; labels not usable for inference. fig/continuation_clock_window.png: row displacement decays during flat price periods while event displacement holds. This motivated the hazard-clock control. fig/continuation_clock_scores.png: large heterogeneous paired deltas and opposite target effects; no visual support for uniform event superiority. fig/continuation_hazard_scores.png: inspected after followup; event advantage over hazard is concentrated in t1 and varies by sequence. No common-clock promotion. METRIC-OPTIMAL ESTIMAND Ignoring prediction clipping, population weighted Pearson is ordinary Pearson under the tilted measure dQ proportional to |clip(Y)| dP. Its optimal predictor is affine to E_Q[clip(Y)|X] = E[|clip(Y)|clip(Y)|X]/E[|clip(Y)||X]. Weighted MSE estimates this ratio; ordinary MSE need not. Prediction clipping and restricted linear function classes break the unrestricted affine optimum. This is a model argument, not evidence that every weighted fit beats an unweighted control. RANKED NEXT DIRECTIONS (NOT RUN OR INTEGRATED)
  1. Separate t0 row-clock and t1 event-clock readouts. Control: same-budget shared clock and two clocks provided to both heads. Falsifier: advantage disappears on controller-defined held-out linked components or versus the strong baseline.
  2. Distinguish realized event age from average hazard. Control: causal rolling hazard clock plus age/intensity features, matched feature count and shrinkage; compare discrete event EMA. Falsifier: discrete event head loses to hazard+age.
  3. Train weighted versus ordinary ridge on identical rows and scaling. Control: fixed penalty and clipping; compare both weighted and unweighted correlations. Falsifier: weighting hurts exact masked WP on untouched components. Avoid fitting mask propensities from this repeatedly exposed validation panel.
  4. Cross-instrument error correction only after a feature-only spread identity and train-estimated stationarity relation are verified. Controls: own-instrument lags and causal delayed i1; falsifier: no incremental held-component WP. Prior near-zero contemporaneous i1 change correlations neither prove nor rule it out.
METHOD SOURCE Clark (1973), A Subordinated Stochastic Process Model with Finite Variance for Speculative Prices, Econometrica 41(1), 135–155: https://www.stats.org.uk/stochastic-processes/Clark1973.pdf Primary paper motivates stochastic activity clocks; it does not prescribe this EMA or establish forecastability here. The hazard adaptation is our inference. DELIVERABLES AND REPRODUCTION scripts/continuation_clock_probe.py and continuation_hazard_probe.py are bounded standalone scripts. Updated eda_econometrics.py displays measured results, sample IDs and PNGs; headless export is checked and saved as continuation_notebook.html. No server remains. STATE.json records commands/phases; HYPOTHESES.json retains the original frozen card and points to HYPOTHESES_followup_frozen.json. Model NPZs, per-sequence CSVs, result JSONs, logs, and artifact SHA256 manifest are under cache/. CUDA unavailable. No resource failure, installs, GPU launch, commits, or external writes by probes.
